old: The thyroid takes up iodide to make its hormones, so I-131 collects there. Its beta particles travel only a few millimeters in tissue, so the dose is delivered mainly to the thyroid. Radioactive decay does not depend on location in the body.
new: The thyroid takes up iodide to make its hormones, so I-131 collects there. Its beta particles travel only about a millimeter or two in tissue, so the dose is delivered mainly to the thyroid. Radioactive decay does not depend on location in the body.
why: I-131 beta particles have a mean tissue range of about 0.5 mm and a maximum of about 2 mm; "a few millimeters" overstates it.

old: [H3O+] = 1 × 10−8 M means pH = 8, the bile bar. Saliva (pH 6.5) has about 3 × 10−7 M and blood (pH 7.4) about 4 × 10−8 M, which is more acidic than 10−8 M, not less: the exponent 8 belongs to pH 8 exactly.
new: [H3O+] = 1 × 10−8 M means pH = 8, the bile bar. Saliva (pH 6.5) has about 3 × 10−7 M and blood (pH 7.4) about 4 × 10−8 M; both have more H3O+ than 1 × 10−8 M, and stomach fluid (pH 1.5) has far more.
